source: Not findings. The ways people actually describe using to reach financial independence, each a composition of levers from data/levers.json — the side hustle, the house hack, the steady raise, a cheaper town, a better job — with Drift, the raise spent, as the baseline everything is measured against. Every figure lives in the lever library, not here; this file only says which levers a way pulls and how hard, and which ways wait for a fact (a remote job, a working life) before they show.
confidenceNote: The paths are a teaching device. No study says a house hack cuts housing by 40% for you; it says it can, and the room lets you change the figure rather than pretending the default is a finding.
note: Read by engines/adventure.js. Never inline a lever figure in a room or in this file: a path is `levers: [{ id, scale }]`, the id a key in data/levers.json and the scale a share of the lever (1 when omitted). `onlyIf` names a lever whose appliesWhen must pass before the path is offered. `baseline: true` marks Drift, the way every other way's delta is measured against. The engine composes the raise, the extra income and the housing cut from the levers and writes each path's assumption sentence from their figures. The house hack reads the real accommodation line (D-172); the share below is a fallback, not a fact. Contingencies are headwinds or tailwinds: same mechanics, separate lists. D-174, D-176.
returnRateSource: The median real return band in data/return_bands.json, so this room and the rest of the app agree.

paths.label: Drift
paths.line: Nothing changes. The raises get spent. This is what every other way is measured against.

paths.label: Steady
paths.line: One job, rising slowly. Save the difference and let it compound.

paths.label: Side Hustle
paths.line: Keep the job, add work of your own on the side.

paths.label: House Hack
paths.line: Attack the largest line instead of the income. Housemate, smaller place, cheaper town.

paths.label: Both, Smaller
paths.line: Half a hustle and half a house hack, because doing two things properly is harder than doing one.

paths.label: Move Somewhere Cheaper
paths.line: Keep the job, work remote, and take a quarter off every needs line.

paths.label: Change Jobs
paths.line: A better-paid job from year one, and the same discipline after it.

contingencies.label: Markets fall 30%
contingencies.line: A 30% drop in year 2, then the usual return resumes.

contingencies.label: Six months without work
contingencies.line: Income stops for half of year 3. Spending continues, paid from cash first; anything a side income earns keeps coming.

contingencies.label: Lifestyle creeps up
contingencies.line: Spending rises 4% a year in real terms on top of everything else.

contingencies.label: A real raise
contingencies.line: A 15% rise in year 2 that you keep saving rather than spending.

accommodationShareFallbackNote: Used ONLY when the accommodation line in Cash Flow is blank: housing is taken as 30% of spending, the common rule of thumb, and the room prints "assumed 30% because accommodation is not filled in" beside the figure. With the line filled in the cut reads the real number. D-172.
